patch.value: MCP pm_comments lists only the newest 20 comments by default: the backward output cursor stops at that producer page and the last page reports has_more without a continuation

Found 2026-11-08 by the CodeRabbit review of PR 1685. A pm_comments MCP listing without limit or full is bounded by the producer to the newest 20 comments (runMcpCommentsAction sets limit 20 and includeMeta), with total_count and has_more true when more exist. A universal output cursor pages only within that producer page. On an item with more than 20 comments, following next_cursor backwards under a small outputBudget therefore stops after the 20th-newest comment. The last page still reports has_more true (from the producer) but carries no next_cursor, so an agent cannot tell how to reach older comments except by restarting with options.limit or options.full true, which the tool description mentions. Expected: when the producer page is exhausted, the envelope names the producer continuation, for example a cursor or a suggested limit for the next older window, so has_more true never arrives without an executable continuation. Duplicate check: searched MCP comments default 20 has_more continuation producer page. pm-gh1679 (open) owns a producer cursor for item history, which is the analogous design, and pm-8s53lj (closed) made the output cursor page backwards within the producer page.

An MCP comments listing whose producer page is exhausted names a continuation to the next older window, or reports has_more only when a continuation is present; A spec drives tools/call on more than 20 comments and reaches the oldest comment by following continuations alone
Through MCP tools/call, list pm_comments on an item with more than 20 comments with a small outputBudget and follow next_cursor until it disappears, then read has_more
has_more true always comes with an executable continuation that reaches older comments beyond the producer page
After the newest 20 comments the page reports has_more true and no next_cursor; only restarting with options.limit or options.full reaches older comments
